tests.title: A clean merge rebases the source and fast-forwards the target
given: a workspace whose target branch and source branch have diverged without conflicting
tests.when: a merge job runs to completion
then: the target holds the source's commits on top of the commits it had
no merge commit was created
base_sha is the target's head before and merged_sha its head after
tests.pseudocode: in the merge job integration test file: j = run_job(); assert parents(head(target)) has length 1 and j.base_sha == before and j.merged_sha == head(target)

tests.title: A job carries the documented fields through its states
given: jobs that complete, fail, are dead-lettered and are cancelled
tests.when: each is read at each stage of its life
then: every job carries the documented fields
base_sha and merged_sha are null until completion and conflict_files is empty without a conflict
the observed statuses are a prefix of queued, running and then one terminal status
tests.pseudocode: in the merge job integration test file, table over the four job outcomes asserting the fields at each stage

tests.title: A merge job waits for the lock instead of being refused
given: a workspace whose lock is held by a long operation
tests.when: a merge is submitted and the lock is later released
then: the submit answers 202 and the job is queued
the job is never answered 409 workspace_busy
the job runs and completes once the lock frees
tests.pseudocode: in the merge job integration test file: hold(lock); assert post(merge).status == 202; release(lock); assert eventually(status(job) == 'completed')

tests.title: A conflicting merge fails and leaves the target alone
given: a source and a target that change the same region differently
tests.when: the merge job runs
then: the job's status is failed
conflict_files names every conflicting path
the target branch holds the head it had before the job
tests.pseudocode: in the merge job integration test file: before = head(target); j = run_job(); assert j.status == 'failed' and head(target) == before

tests.title: A valid merge submit queues a job
given: a ready workspace with a target branch and a source branch
tests.when: the merge is submitted
then: the response is 202 with the job at status queued
the job carries its id, the target, the source and the submitting user
tests.pseudocode: in the merge routes' integration test file: r = post(merges, body); assert r.status == 202 and r.json.status == 'queued'

tests.title: A malformed submit is refused before the workspace is considered
given: a ready workspace, an unready one, and a slug the caller cannot see
tests.when: submits are made with a malformed body, a missing target, a missing source, a name with a leading hyphen, a name containing two dots, a branch that does not exist, and a malformed name against the invisible slug
then: each answers 400 and queues nothing
the malformed name against the invisible slug answers 400 rather than 404, because the body is checked first
the unready workspace answers 400
tests.pseudocode: in the merge routes' test file, table over the cases asserting 400 and the job count

tests.title: A duplicate merge is refused
given: a queued merge of one source into one target
tests.when: the same source and target are submitted again, the same source into a different target, and the same pair again after the first completes
then: the duplicate answers 409 with error_type duplicate_merge and the existing job is unaffected
the different target is accepted
the pair is accepted again once the first job has completed
tests.pseudocode: in the merge routes' integration test file: assert post(same).json.error.error_type == 'duplicate_merge' and post(otherTarget).status == 202

tests.title: Jobs are listed and read, capped at 200
given: a workspace with 205 merge jobs, another with none, and a job belonging to a different workspace
tests.when: the jobs are listed for each workspace, one is read, the foreign job is read and an unknown id is read
then: the list answers 200 with at most 200 entries
the empty workspace answers an empty array
the read answers 200 with the job
the foreign job and the unknown id both answer 404
tests.pseudocode: in the merge routes' test file: assert len(get(merges).json) == 200 and get(merges, foreignId).status == 404

tests.title: A queued job is cancelled and never runs
given: a queued merge job on a workspace whose lock is held so it has not started
tests.when: the job is cancelled and the lock is then released
then: the cancel answers 200 with status cancelled
the job does not run after the lock frees
the target branch is untouched
tests.pseudocode: in the merge routes' integration test file: delete(job); release(lock); assert status(job) == 'cancelled' and head(target) == before

tests.title: Cancelling a job that is not queued is refused
given: jobs at running, completed, failed, dead_letter and cancelled
tests.when: each is cancelled
then: each answers 409
each job's status is unchanged
tests.pseudocode: in the merge routes' test file, table over the five statuses asserting 409 and an unchanged status

tests.title: A dead-lettered job is requeued unless a duplicate is live
given: a dead-lettered job, jobs at every other status, and a dead-lettered job whose source and target are already queued elsewhere
tests.when: each is requeued
then: the dead-lettered job answers 200 with status queued
every other status answers 409
the one whose pair is already live answers 409
tests.pseudocode: in the merge routes' test file, table over (status, duplicateLive, expected)

tests.title: A batch rebase answers one result per branch, in order
given: a ready workspace with three branches that all rebase cleanly onto the target
tests.when: a batch rebase is requested
then: the response is 200 with three results in the order the branches were given
each result is ok with the branch's new head
each branch is at that head afterwards
tests.pseudocode: in the batch rebase integration test file: r = post(rebase, [a,b,c]); assert [x.branch for x in r.json.results] == [a,b,c] and all(x.status == 'ok')

tests.title: A conflicting branch does not stop the others
given: three branches of which the second conflicts with the target
tests.when: a batch rebase is requested
then: three results are returned
the second is a conflict with its conflicting files
the first and third are rebased and are at their new heads
tests.pseudocode: in the batch rebase integration test file: r = post(rebase, [a,b,c]); assert r.json.results[1].status == 'conflict' and head(a) == r.json.results[0].new_head

tests.title: A malformed batch rebase is refused whole
given: a ready workspace, an unready one and a slug the caller cannot see
tests.when: requests are made with a malformed body, no target ref, an empty branch list, an invalid name in the second position, 21 branches, against the unready workspace, and with a malformed name against the invisible slug
then: each answers 400 and rebases nothing
the invalid name's message names its index
the malformed name against the invisible slug answers 400 rather than 404
tests.pseudocode: in the batch rebase test file, table over the cases asserting 400 and that no branch moved

tests.title: A busy workspace and a failed rebase leave no branch part way
given: a workspace whose lock is held, and an engine made to fail part way through the second of three branches
tests.when: a batch rebase is requested against each
then: the held lock answers 409 with error_type workspace_busy and moves nothing
the failure answers 500
every branch is either at its new head or at the head it had before
tests.pseudocode: in the batch rebase test file: assert post(rebase).json.error.error_type == 'workspace_busy'; with engine failing assert every branch head in {before, after}

tests.title: A job survives a restart of whatever runs it
given: a merge job running when its component is restarted, and one queued when its component is evicted
tests.when: the component restarts and the jobs are read
then: each job's status is queued, completed or failed
no job is left at running with nothing running it
no job is dropped
tests.pseudocode: in the merge job integration test file: start(job); restart(); assert status(job) in {'queued','completed','failed'}

tests.title: A stalled job is dead-lettered and can be requeued
given: a merge job made to stop making progress, and a controllable clock
tests.when: the clock is advanced past 15 minutes and the job is then requeued
then: the job's status becomes dead_letter with its retry count recorded
the requeue answers 200 and returns it to queued
it is not retried for ever in between
tests.pseudocode: in the merge job integration test file: stall(job); clock.advance(16*60); assert status(job) == 'dead_letter'; assert post(requeue).json.status == 'queued'

tests.title: The target branch is never left at an intermediate head
given: merge jobs interrupted before the rebase, during it and between the rebase and the fast-forward
tests.when: each interruption happens and the target is read
then: the target holds either the head it had before or the merged result
it never holds an intermediate commit
a requeued job reaches one of the two
tests.pseudocode: in the merge job integration test file, table over the interruption points asserting head(target) in {before, merged}

tests.title: A branch is merged through the queue against a running deployment
given: a running deployment, a workspace with a target branch and an agent branch pushed to Parley
tests.when: afc merge submit --wait is run
then: the command exits 0 and prints the job at completed
the target branch holds the agent's commits on top of its own
base_sha and merged_sha are reported
tests.pseudocode: in the merge smoke test file: r = run('afc merge submit --source feature --target main --wait'); assert r.exit == 0 and json(r.stdout).status == 'completed'

tests.title: A conflicting merge is reported and the target untouched
given: a running deployment and a branch that conflicts with the target
tests.when: afc merge submit --wait is run and then afc merge status
then: the submit exits 1 because the job ended failed
the status output names the conflicting files
the target branch is at the head it had before
tests.pseudocode: in the merge smoke test file: r = run('afc merge submit --wait'); assert r.exit == 1; assert json(run('afc merge status').stdout).conflict_files

tests.title: Several branches are rebased in one request against a running deployment
given: a running deployment and three branches, one of which conflicts with the target
tests.when: afc rebase submit is run with the three branches
then: the command prints three results in order
two carry new heads and one carries conflicting files
the two rebased branches are at their reported heads
tests.pseudocode: in the merge smoke test file: r = run('afc rebase submit --target-ref main --branches a,b,c'); assert len(json(r.stdout).results) == 3
